page.title: What I Can Get
page.purpose: Show a holder everything their tokens buy, make affordability obvious before they try, and let them redeem in one clear action.

priorities.statement: Whether an item is affordable right now is understood before any interaction.
priorities.notes: A child tapping a reward they cannot afford and being refused is a bad experience the layout should prevent.

priorities.statement: The cost of each reward is as prominent as its name.
Whether a reward needs a grown-up's approval is stated before redeeming, not after.
priorities.notes: Surprise is the failure mode here: a holder who expects something instantly and gets a pending state feels denied.

priorities.statement: Unavailable rewards are visible but clearly out of reach, rather than hidden.
priorities.notes: Hiding them makes the catalog feel arbitrary; showing them with a reason makes the economy legible.

states.description: Catalog entries listed with affordability and approval posture resolved.
The minter has declared no rewards yet; the page explains that rather than showing a blank list.
Catalog loaded but the holder's balance failed; entries render with affordability unknown and say so.
Redemption settled immediately; the holder is told what they received.
Redemption is queued for minter approval; the holder is told plainly that it is waiting and why.
Redemption refused by a rule; the refusal names the rule in language the holder can act on.
No connection; the catalog is shown from cache and redeeming is disabled with a stated reason.
Showing a cached catalog after a failed refresh; affordability may be out of date and says so.

claims.statement: Affordability is communicated on each entry before any interaction, by text and not by color alone.
An entry requiring approval says so before the redeem action is taken.
The pending state is clearly distinguishable from the success state; a queued redemption never reads as completed.
The validation-error state names the rule that refused and what would change it, never a generic failure.
Unavailable entries remain present in the list with a stated reason rather than being filtered out.
Each entry reads name then cost, with cost given equal typographic weight.
Redeeming is fully operable by keyboard and announced to screen readers.
